name: zkvm_sp1
description: The SP1 platform: entry point and memory map

options.note: Elide the RA spill/reload and frame in leaf methods (dotnet-riscv patches 23 and 31). Sound only on a single-threaded deterministic guest with no GC thread suspension and no return-address hijacking.

The decoder has no C extension, and a single-threaded guest needs no atomics: the managed .text stays 32-bit and lock-free (dotnet-riscv fixups 24/25). Check with --error-on-compressed / --error-on-atomic.

Per-site inline allocation (dotnet-riscv fixup 26): the cell of the bump pointer, at a fixed address. It MUST equal g_zk_bump_ptr in the linker script. SP1's space runs to 2^48; its RAM stays up to 0xbfff0000, and the cell is 8 bytes below it.

SP1 asserts natural alignment and fails the execution on a violation (InvalidMemoryAccess for any LH/LW/LD/SH/SW/SD off its boundary, crates/core/executor/src/vm.rs), so its guests are always built byte-wise (dotnet-riscv fixup 35).
And every access that the JIT cannot prove aligned gets an inline alignment test with a wide fast path and a byte-wise slow path.

postlink.note: SP1 transpiles every word of every executable segment before it runs anything, and faults on the first one it cannot decode. FENCE (an illegal instruction for SP1; a single-hart guest has nothing to order) and the all-zero padding that ILC puts between methods are unreachable but fatal there, so both become NOP.
